Write G(x) := graphPoint x (u x) = (x, u(x)), Gamma := graphOver u (Bo^n_R(0)) = G(Bo^n_R(0)), H^n := muHE[n], omega_n := unitBallVolume n, B_r closed and Bo_r open balls. Assume (graph) Q((S - xi)) cap Bo_R(0) = Gamma cap Bo_R(0), and (C4) for every x in Bo^n_R(0), H^n(Gamma cap B_r(G(x))) / ofReal(omega_n r^n) -> 1 in [0,inf] as r -> 0+. Then (a) H^n(S cap Bo_rho(xi)) < inf for every real rho < R, and (b) for every y in S cap Bo_R(xi), H^n(S cap B_r(y)) / ofReal(omega_n r^n) -> 1 as r -> 0+.

Source: steps 1-2 of the parent-supplied proof (finite graph piece; density of nu at its points), generalized from Bo_{R/2}(xi) to every Bo_rho(xi) with rho < R and to every point of S cap Bo_R(xi), with the sibling C^1-graph density theorem entering only through hypothesis (C4).
0. Preliminaries. (i) graphPoint is linear in the pair: graphPoint (a + a') (b + b') = graphPoint a b + graphPoint a' b' and graphPoint (c a) (c b) = c graphPoint a b (coordinatewise identities of Fin.append); in particular graphPoint a b - graphPoint a' b' = graphPoint (a - a') (b - b'). (ii) Norm identity: ||graphPoint a b||^2 = sum over i < n+l of (Fin.append a b)_i^2 = sum_{i<n} a_i^2 + sum_{j<l} b_j^2 = ||a||^2 + ||b||^2 (split the sum over Fin (n+l) into the first n and the last l indices, Fin.sum_univ_add, Fin.append_left, Fin.append_right). Hence ||a|| <= ||graphPoint a b|| <= ||a|| + ||b||. (iii) Let T(z) := Q(z - xi). T is an isometric bijection of R^(n+l) (translation followed by the linear isometry equivalence Q), ||T z|| = ||z - xi||, ||T z - T z'|| = ||z - z'||, and T(X) = Q '' ((fun x => x - xi) '' X) for every X. Since T is an isometry, H^n(T(X)) = H^n(X) for every X (Mathlib Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image). The hypothesis (graph) reads T(S) cap Bo_R(0) = Gamma cap Bo_R(0).
1. Proof of (a). Let rho < R. If rho <= 0 then Bo_rho(xi) is empty and H^n(empty) = 0 < inf. Assume 0 < rho < R and let K := B^n_rho(0), the closed ball of R^n.
1a. T(S cap Bo_rho(xi)) is contained in G(K): if z in S and ||z - xi|| < rho, then T z in T(S) and ||T z|| = ||z - xi|| < rho < R, so T z in T(S) cap Bo_R(0) = Gamma cap Bo_R(0); write T z = G(x) with x in Bo^n_R(0). By (ii), ||x|| <= ||G(x)|| = ||T z|| < rho, so x in K.
1b. G is Lipschitz on K. K is compact, convex and contained in the open ball Bo^n_R(0) because rho < R. Since u is C^1 on the open set Bo^n_R(0), u is differentiable at every point of it and x -> Du(x) is continuous there (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen); hence ||Du|| is bounded on the compact set K by some C >= 0, and by the mean value inequality on the convex set K (Convex.lipschitzOnWith_of_nnnorm_fderiv_le), ||u(a) - u(b)|| <= C ||a - b|| for a, b in K. By (i) and (ii), ||G(a) - G(b)|| = ||graphPoint (a - b) (u a - u b)|| <= ||a - b|| + ||u(a) - u(b)|| <= (1 + C) ||a - b|| for a, b in K.
1c. muHE[n] = c_n muH[n] with the constant c_n = addHaarScalarFactor volume muH[n] (on EuclideanSpace R (Fin n)) independent of the ambient space (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def). For a (1 + C)-Lipschitz map on K, muH[n](G(K)) <= (1 + C)^n muH[n](K) (LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le with d = n >= 0), hence H^n(G(K)) <= (1 + C)^n H^n(K). On R^n, H^n = muHE[n] equals Lebesgue measure (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume) and the closed ball K has finite Lebesgue measure, so H^n(G(K)) < inf.
1d. By (iii), 1a, monotonicity and 1c: H^n(S cap Bo_rho(xi)) = H^n(T(S cap Bo_rho(xi))) <= H^n(G(K)) < inf.
2. Proof of (b). Let y in S cap Bo_R(xi) and delta := R - ||y - xi|| > 0.
2a. T y in T(S) and ||T y|| = ||y - xi|| < R, so T y in T(S) cap Bo_R(0) = Gamma cap Bo_R(0) and T y = G(x) for some x in Bo^n_R(0).
2b. Claim: T(S cap B_r(y)) = Gamma cap B_r(G(x)) for 0 < r < delta. (Inclusion one) If z in S with ||z - y|| <= r, then ||T z - G(x)|| = ||T z - T y|| = ||z - y|| <= r and ||T z|| = ||z - xi|| <= ||z - y|| + ||y - xi|| <= r + ||y - xi|| < R; so T z in T(S) cap Bo_R(0) = Gamma cap Bo_R(0), hence T z in Gamma cap B_r(G(x)). (Inclusion two) If w in Gamma with ||w - G(x)|| <= r, then ||w|| <= ||G(x)|| + r = ||y - xi|| + r < R, so w in Gamma cap Bo_R(0) = T(S) cap Bo_R(0); write w = T z with z in S; then ||z - y|| = ||T z - T y|| = ||w - G(x)|| <= r, so z in S cap B_r(y) and w in T(S cap B_r(y)).
2c. By (iii) and 2b, H^n(S cap B_r(y)) = H^n(Gamma cap B_r(G(x))) for every r in (0, delta). The interval (0, delta) belongs to the filter nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0), so the functions r -> H^n(S cap B_r(y)) / ofReal(omega_n r^n) and r -> H^n(Gamma cap B_r(G(x))) / ofReal(omega_n r^n) are eventually equal along r -> 0+ (Tendsto.congr'). By (C4) at x in Bo^n_R(0) the second tends to 1; hence so does the first. This proves (b).

subproblems.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, U a subset of R^(n+l), V a rectifiable n-varifold in U (contract structure RectifiableVarifold n l U) with weight mu := V.weight and support Sigma := V.support = U cap spt mu, xi in R^(n+l), R real with Bo_R(xi) contained in U, Q a linear isometry equivalence of R^(n+l), u : R^n -> R^l differentiable on Bo^n_R(0), G(z) := graphPoint z (u z), and assume Q((Sigma - xi)) cap Bo_R(0) = G(Bo^n_R(0)) cap Bo_R(0). Assume (TP): for mu-a.e. y in Bo_R(xi) and every x in Bo^n_R(0) with Q(y - xi) = G(x), V.tangentProj y is the orthogonal projection (starProjection) onto the subspace Q^{-1}(range DG(x)), DG(x) := fderiv R G x. Then for mu-a.e. y in Bo_R(xi) there is a subspace P of R^(n+l) with finrank P = n and V.tangentProj y = P.starProjection.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ n ℓ : ℕ, ∀ (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (ξ : Amb n ℓ) (R : ℝ) (Q : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ) (u : Rn n → Rn ℓ), ball ξ R ⊆ U → DifferentiableOn ℝ u (ball 0 R) → Q '' ((fun x => x - ξ) '' V.support) ∩ ball 0 R = graphOver u (ball 0 R) ∩ ball 0 R → (∀ᵐ y ∂V.weight, y ∈ ball ξ R → ∀ x ∈ ball (0 : Rn n) R, Q (y - ξ) = graphPoint x (u x) → V.tangentProj y = (Submodule.map Q.symm.toLinearEquiv.toLinearMap (LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ (fun z : Rn n => graphPoint z (u z)) x).toLinearMap)).starProjection) → ∀ᵐ y ∂V.weight, y ∈ ball ξ R → ∃ P : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ), Module.finrank ℝ P = n ∧ V.tangentProj y = P.starProjection
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the (TP) paragraph of the parent-supplied proof ('this subspace has dimension n because DG(x) v = (v, Du(x) v) is injective ... for mu-a.e. y in Bo_R(xi) there is an n-dimensional subspace P with V.tangentProj y = P.starProjection').
1. mu((spt mu)^c) = 0 (Mathlib Measure.measure_compl_support; R^(n+l) is second countable, hence hereditarily Lindelof). Combining with (TP), for mu-a.e. y both y in spt mu and the (TP) implication hold at y. Fix such a y with y in Bo_R(xi); we produce P.
2. y in Bo_R(xi), which is contained in U, and y in spt mu, so y in Sigma = U cap spt mu. Hence Q(y - xi) in Q((Sigma - xi)), and ||Q(y - xi)|| = ||y - xi|| < R, so Q(y - xi) in Q((Sigma - xi)) cap Bo_R(0) = G(Bo^n_R(0)) cap Bo_R(0). Thus there is x in Bo^n_R(0) with G(x) = Q(y - xi).
3. By (TP) at y and this x, V.tangentProj y = P.starProjection with P := Q^{-1}(range D), D := fderiv R G x (P is the image of range D under the linear equivalence Q.symm).
4. G is differentiable at x and D v = graphPoint v (Du(x) v). Let iota1(a) := graphPoint a 0 and iota2(b) := graphPoint 0 b; they are linear maps (coordinatewise identities of Fin.append) between finite-dimensional spaces, hence continuous linear maps, and graphPoint a b = iota1 a + iota2 b, so G = iota1 + iota2 o u. As Bo^n_R(0) is open and u is differentiable on it, u is differentiable at x; by the chain rule G is differentiable at x with D = iota1 + iota2 o Du(x).
5. D is injective. Let pi : R^(n+l) -> R^n be the linear projection onto the first n coordinates, pi(w)_i := w_(Fin.castAdd l i). Then pi(graphPoint a b) = a (Fin.append_left), so pi o iota1 = id and pi o iota2 = 0. Hence pi(D v) = v for every v in R^n, and D v = 0 implies v = 0.
6. finrank (range D) = finrank R^n = n (LinearMap.finrank_range_of_inj and finrank (EuclideanSpace R (Fin n)) = n). Since Q.symm is a linear equivalence, finrank P = finrank (map Q.symm (range D)) = finrank (range D) = n (LinearEquiv.finrank_map_eq). Thus P is n-dimensional and V.tangentProj y = P.starProjection, which proves the claim for mu-a.e. y in Bo_R(xi).

Q(y - xi) lies on the graph: Q(y - xi) = G(x) with x in Bo^n_R(0)
DG(x) v = (v, Du(x) v) is injective because the first-n-coordinates projection inverts it
rank of range DG(x) is n and is preserved by the linear equivalence Q^{-1}

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the monotonicity part of steps 5 and 7 of the parent-supplied proof (Lambda(t) := max{t^(1-n/p) A^(1/p)/kappa, t}; (M) applies at z with R' := t; omega_n Theta(z) <= Phi_z(r) <= e^Lambda r^(-n) mu(B_r(z)) + Lambda), stated once uniformly for all centres in Bo_{R/2}(xi); the sibling monotonicity theorem enters only through hypothesis (hM).
1. Constants. Since n >= 0 and p > n we have p > 0, kappa = (p - n)/(4p) > 0 and beta := 1 - n/p in (0, 1]. Let A := lintegral over B_R(xi) of ||H||^p dmu; A < inf by (hLp), so A^(1/p) < inf (1/p >= 0); put a := (A^(1/p)).toReal >= 0, so A^(1/p) = ofReal(a).
2. Define Lambda(t) := max(t^beta * a / kappa, t) (real rpow). As t -> 0+, t^beta -> 0^beta = 0 (beta > 0; Real.continuousAt_rpow_const), so t^beta a / kappa -> 0 and t -> 0, hence Lambda(t) -> max(0, 0) = 0. For t > 0, Lambda(t) >= t > 0.
3. Choice of t1. Since Lambda(t) -> 0 as t -> 0+, there is eps0 > 0 with Lambda(t) <= 1 for all t in (0, eps0). Put t1 := min(R/8, eps0/2) > 0. Then 0 < Lambda(t) <= 1 for every t in (0, t1].
4. Geometry. Let y in Bo_{R/2}(xi), t in (0, t1] and z in B_t(y). For w in B_t(z): |w - xi| <= |w - z| + |z - y| + |y - xi| < t + t + R/2 <= R/4 + R/2 < R. Hence B_t(z) is contained in Bo_R(xi), which is contained in B_R(xi), contained in U; also Bo_t(z) is contained in Bo_R(xi).
5. Hypotheses of (hM) at (y', R', Lambda) := (z, t, Lambda(t)). (i) t > 0 and B_t(z) contained in U (step 4). (ii) Tangent planes: by (hTP), for mu-a.e. x, x in Bo_R(xi) implies the n-dimensional starProjection property; as Bo_t(z) is contained in Bo_R(xi), the same a.e. statement holds for x in Bo_t(z) (Filter.Eventually.mono). (iii) Measurability: mu restricted to Bo_t(z) is <= mu restricted to Bo_R(xi) (Measure.restrict_mono), so a.e.-strong measurability passes down (AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_measure). (iv) 0 < Lambda(t) <= 1 (step 3). (v) Scaled L^p bound: V.scaledLpNorm H p z t = (ofReal(t^(p-n)) * I)^(1/p) with I := lintegral over B_t(z) of ||H||^p dmu <= A, because B_t(z) is contained in B_R(xi) (lintegral_mono_set). As s -> s^(1/p) is monotone on [0, inf] (1/p > 0), scaledLpNorm <= (ofReal(t^(p-n)) * A)^(1/p) = ofReal(t^(p-n))^(1/p) * A^(1/p) (ENNReal.mul_rpow_of_nonneg) = ofReal((t^(p-n))^(1/p)) * ofReal(a) (ENNReal.ofReal_rpow_of_nonneg) = ofReal(t^((p-n)/p) * a) (Real.rpow_mul for t >= 0, ENNReal.ofReal_mul) = ofReal(t^beta * a), since (p - n)/p = 1 - n/p. Because Lambda(t) >= t^beta a / kappa and kappa > 0, t^beta a <= kappa Lambda(t); so scaledLpNorm <= ofReal(kappa * Lambda(t)) = ofReal((p - n)/(4p) * Lambda(t)).
6. Apply (hM) at (z, t, Lambda(t)): we obtain F with |F(r) - 1| <= Lambda(t) and F(r) <= exp(Lambda(t)) for r in (0, t), Phi(r) := F(r) r^(-n) mu(B_r(z)) + F(r) - 1 nondecreasing on (0, t), and Theta >= 0 with V.HasDensity z Theta and Phi(r) -> omega_n Theta as r -> 0+.
7. For r in (0, t): omega_n Theta <= Phi(r). Indeed for every r' in (0, r) both r', r lie in (0, t) and r' <= r, so Phi(r') <= Phi(r); the interval (0, r) belongs to nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0), so Phi(r') <= Phi(r) eventually as r' -> 0+, and passing to the limit (le_of_tendsto) gives omega_n Theta <= Phi(r).
8. For r in (0, t): Phi(r) <= exp(Lambda(t)) r^(-n) mu(B_r(z)) + Lambda(t). Indeed r^(-n) mu(B_r(z)) >= 0 (toReal is nonnegative) and F(r) <= exp(Lambda(t)), so F(r) r^(-n) mu(B_r(z)) <= exp(Lambda(t)) r^(-n) mu(B_r(z)); and F(r) - 1 <= |F(r) - 1| <= Lambda(t).
9. Steps 6-8 give, for the arbitrary y in Bo_{R/2}(xi), t in (0, t1] and z in B_t(y), a real Theta >= 0 with V.HasDensity z Theta and omega_n Theta <= exp(Lambda(t)) r^(-n) mu(B_r(z)) + Lambda(t) for all r in (0, t); t1 and Lambda (steps 2-3) do not depend on y, t, z, and Lambda(t) -> 0 as t -> 0+ (step 2).
proof_key_steps: A := integral of |H|^p over B_R(xi) is finite; Lambda(t) := max(t^(1-n/p) A^(1/p)/kappa, t) tends to 0 and is positive
t1 <= R/8 with Lambda <= 1 on (0, t1]; then B_t(z) lies in Bo_R(xi) for z in B_t(y), y in Bo_{R/2}(xi)
tangent-plane and measurability hypotheses restrict to sub-balls; scaledLpNorm z t <= t^(1-n/p) A^(1/p) <= kappa Lambda(t)

subproblems.title: Upper semicontinuity of the density under a monotonicity bound with vanishing error
subproblems.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, U a subset of R^(n+l), V a rectifiable n-varifold in U with weight mu, y in R^(n+l), t1 > 0 and Lambda : R -> R with Lambda(t) -> 0 as t -> 0+; mu(B_r(z)) means (V.weight (closedBall z r)).toReal and omega_n := unitBallVolume n. Assume (hmon): for every t in (0, t1] and every z in B_t(y) there is a real Theta >= 0 with V.HasDensity z Theta and omega_n Theta <= exp(Lambda(t)) r^(-n) mu(B_r(z)) + Lambda(t) for all r in (0, t). Let Theta_y >= 0 with V.HasDensity y Theta_y, and let c > Theta_y. Then there is d > 0 such that every z in B_d(y) has some real Theta < c with V.HasDensity z Theta.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ n ℓ : ℕ, ∀ (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (y : Amb n ℓ) (t₁ : ℝ) (Λ : ℝ → ℝ), 0 < t₁ → Tendsto Λ (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0) → (∀ t ∈ Ioc 0 t₁, ∀ z ∈ closedBall y t, ∃ Θ : ℝ, 0 ≤ Θ ∧ V.HasDensity z Θ ∧ ∀ r ∈ Ioo 0 t, unitBallVolume n * Θ ≤ Real.exp (Λ t) * (r ^ n)⁻¹ * (V.weight (closedBall z r)).toReal + Λ t) → ∀ Θy : ℝ, 0 ≤ Θy → V.HasDensity y Θy → ∀ c : ℝ, Θy < c → ∃ d > 0, ∀ z ∈ closedBall y d, ∃ Θ : ℝ, Θ < c ∧ V.HasDensity z Θ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the core of step 5 of the parent-supplied proof ('Theta(z) <= c < 1 for every z with |z - y| <= eps t', obtained from monotonicity at z, the inclusion B_r(z) in B_{r+d}(y) and the density at y) and of step 7 ('Theta < 2 near xi'), written for an arbitrary level c > Theta_y; the limit r -> t- of the parent is replaced by the fixed radius r = t/2.
1. omega := omega_n = pi^(n/2)/Gamma(n/2 + 1) > 0, because pi > 0 (so pi^(n/2) > 0) and Gamma > 0 on (0, inf).
2. Put b := Theta_y + (c - Theta_y)/3 and a' := Theta_y + 2(c - Theta_y)/3, so 0 <= Theta_y < b < a' < c and b > 0. Since (1 + 2 eps)^n -> 1 as eps -> 0, choose eps in (0, 1/2] with (1 + 2 eps)^n b <= a', and put a := (1 + 2 eps)^n b; then a <= a' < c.
3. Mass bound at y. By V.HasDensity y Theta_y, mu(B_s(y)) / ofReal(omega s^n) -> ofReal(Theta_y) in [0, inf] as s -> 0+, and ofReal(Theta_y) < ofReal(b) because Theta_y < b and b > 0. Hence there is sigma1 > 0 such that for every s in (0, sigma1), mu(B_s(y)) / ofReal(omega s^n) < ofReal(b); since 0 < ofReal(omega s^n) < inf, this gives (ENNReal.div_lt_iff) V.weight(B_s(y)) < ofReal(b) * ofReal(omega s^n) = ofReal(b omega s^n).
4. Choice of t. As t -> 0+, exp(Lambda(t)) a + Lambda(t)/omega -> exp(0) a + 0 = a < c (continuity of exp and Lambda(t) -> 0). The three conditions 0 < t <= t1, t < sigma1, exp(Lambda(t)) a + Lambda(t)/omega < c each hold eventually in the nontrivial filter nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0), so some t satisfies all of them. Put d := eps t > 0.
5. Let z in B_d(y). Since d = eps t <= t/2 < t, z in B_t(y) and t in (0, t1], so (hmon) gives a real Theta >= 0 with V.HasDensity z Theta and omega Theta <= exp(Lambda(t)) r^(-n) mu(B_r(z)) + Lambda(t) for r in (0, t). Use r := t/2.
6. Let s := t/2 + d = (t/2)(1 + 2 eps). Then 0 < s <= t/2 + t/2 = t < sigma1, and B_{t/2}(z) is contained in B_s(y) (|w - y| <= |w - z| + |z - y| <= t/2 + d). By monotonicity and step 3, V.weight(B_{t/2}(z)) <= V.weight(B_s(y)) <= ofReal(b omega s^n), so the real number mu(B_{t/2}(z)) satisfies mu(B_{t/2}(z)) <= b omega s^n = b omega (t/2)^n (1 + 2 eps)^n = omega a (t/2)^n (ENNReal.toReal_le_of_le_ofReal). Therefore (t/2)^(-n) mu(B_{t/2}(z)) <= omega a.
7. Since exp(Lambda(t)) > 0, steps 5-6 give omega Theta <= exp(Lambda(t)) omega a + Lambda(t); dividing by omega > 0, Theta <= exp(Lambda(t)) a + Lambda(t)/omega < c by step 4. Thus z has the real Theta < c with V.HasDensity z Theta. As z in B_d(y) was arbitrary, d works.
proof_key_steps: choose b in (Theta_y, c) and eps with a := (1 + 2 eps)^n b < c
density at y gives mu(B_s(y)) <= b omega s^n for s < sigma1
choose t <= t1, t < sigma1 with exp(Lambda(t)) a + Lambda(t)/omega < c, and d := eps t
for z in B_d(y): monotonicity bound at r = t/2 and B_{t/2}(z) in B_{t/2 + d}(y) give Theta(z) <= exp(Lambda(t)) a + Lambda(t)/omega < c

subproblems.title: Density equals multiplicity a.e. where the support has unit density (Besicovitch differentiation)
subproblems.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, U a subset of R^(n+l), V = v(M, theta) a rectifiable n-varifold in U (M := V.carrier, theta := V.mult, mu := V.weight = (H^n restricted to M).withDensity (ofReal o theta), Sigma := V.support = U cap spt mu, H^n := muHE[n]), y0 in R^(n+l) and r0 real with B_{r0}(y0) contained in U; O := Bo_{r0}(y0). Assume H^n(Sigma cap O) < inf and, for every y in Sigma cap O, H^n(Sigma cap B_r(y)) / ofReal(omega_n r^n) -> 1 as r -> 0+. Then (a) for mu-a.e. y, y in O implies V.HasDensity y theta(y); and (b) for almost every y with respect to H^n restricted to Sigma cap O, y not in M implies V.HasDensity y 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ n ℓ : ℕ, ∀ (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (y₀ : Amb n ℓ) (r₀ : ℝ), closedBall y₀ r₀ ⊆ U → (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) (V.support ∩ ball y₀ r₀) < ⊤ → (∀ y ∈ V.support ∩ ball y₀ r₀, Tendsto (fun r : ℝ => (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) (V.support ∩ closedBall y r) / ENNReal.ofReal (unitBallVolume n * r ^ n)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 1)) → (∀ᵐ y ∂V.weight, y ∈ ball y₀ r₀ → V.HasDensity y (V.mult y)) ∧ ∀ᵐ y ∂((μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)).restrict (V.support ∩ ball y₀ r₀)), y ∉ V.carrier → V.HasDensity y 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3-4 of the parent-supplied proof and the differentiation part of step 6(b) (Besicovitch differentiation of lambda := mu restricted to O with respect to nu := H^n restricted to Sigma cap O, combined with the unit density of nu).
1. Measurability and finiteness. spt mu is closed, O is open and O is contained in B_{r0}(y0), contained in U; hence Sigma cap O = spt mu cap O is a Borel set. nu := H^n restricted to Sigma cap O is a finite Borel measure (total mass H^n(Sigma cap O) < inf). lambda := mu restricted to O is finite: mu(O) <= mu(B_{r0}(y0)) = lintegral over B_{r0}(y0) of ofReal(theta) d(H^n restricted to M) = lintegral over M cap B_{r0}(y0) of ofReal(theta) dH^n <= lintegral over M cap B_{r0}(y0) of |theta| dH^n < inf, because B_{r0}(y0) is a compact subset of U and theta is H^n-integrable on M cap K for every compact K contained in U (structure field integrableOn_mult). Finite measures are locally finite and sigma-finite.
2. mu((spt mu)^c) = 0 (Measure.measure_compl_support), so mu(S cap O) = mu(S cap O cap spt mu) for every set S, and S cap O cap spt mu = S cap (Sigma cap O).
3. lambda = nu.withDensity f, where f(x) := ofReal(M.indicator theta x) = 1_M(x) ofReal(theta(x)). f is AEMeasurable for H^n (M is H^n-null-measurable and theta is AEMeasurable for H^n restricted to M, so M.indicator theta is AEMeasurable for H^n by aemeasurable_indicator_iff_0), hence for nu. For a Borel set S: lambda(S) = mu(S cap O) = mu(S cap O cap spt mu) (step 2) = lintegral over S cap O cap spt mu of ofReal(theta) d(H^n restricted to M) (withDensity_apply) = lintegral over S cap O cap spt mu of 1_M ofReal(theta) dH^n (restriction to the null-measurable set M equals integration of the M-indicator, lintegral_indicator_0) = lintegral over S of f dnu = (nu.withDensity f)(S). Two measures agreeing on all Borel sets are equal.
4. Besicovitch. R^(n+l) is a finite-dimensional normed space: second countable, Borel, with the Besicovitch covering property. By Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_rnDeriv (lambda, nu locally finite), for nu-a.e. y, lambda(B_r(y)) / nu(B_r(y)) -> (lambda.rnDeriv nu)(y) as r -> 0+. By step 3 and Measure.rnDeriv_withDensity_0 (nu sigma-finite, f AEMeasurable), lambda.rnDeriv nu = f nu-a.e. Also nu-a.e. y lies in the Borel set Sigma cap O (ae_restrict_mem). Hence for nu-a.e. y: y in Sigma cap O and lambda(B_r(y)) / nu(B_r(y)) -> f(y).
5. Fix such a y and let delta := r0 - |y - y0| > 0. For 0 < r < delta, B_r(y) is contained in O, so nu(B_r(y)) = H^n(B_r(y) cap Sigma cap O) = H^n(Sigma cap B_r(y)) and lambda(B_r(y)) = mu(B_r(y) cap O) = mu(B_r(y)). By hypothesis q(r) := nu(B_r(y)) / ofReal(omega_n r^n) -> 1; hence q(r) > 1/2 for small r, so nu(B_r(y)) is nonzero, and nu(B_r(y)) <= nu(R^(n+l)) < inf. For such r, mu(B_r(y)) / ofReal(omega_n r^n) = [lambda(B_r(y)) / nu(B_r(y))] * q(r) (cancel the nonzero finite factor nu(B_r(y)) in [0, inf]). The limits are f(y) (finite) and 1, so by ENNReal.Tendsto.mul the product tends to f(y) * 1 = ofReal(M.indicator theta y). Thus V.HasDensity y (M.indicator theta y) for nu-a.e. y.
6. Conclusion (b): for nu-a.e. y with y not in M, M.indicator theta y = 0, so V.HasDensity y 0.
7. Conclusion (a): lambda = nu.withDensity f is absolutely continuous with respect to nu (withDensity_absolutelyContinuous), so the conclusion of step 5 holds lambda-a.e., i.e. for mu-a.e. y, y in O implies V.HasDensity y (M.indicator theta y) (ae_restrict_iff' for the Borel set O). Moreover mu(M^c) = 0, because mu is absolutely continuous with respect to H^n restricted to M, which is concentrated on the null-measurable set M (ae_restrict_mem_0). On M, M.indicator theta = theta. Hence for mu-a.e. y, y in O implies V.HasDensity y theta(y).
proof_key_steps: nu := H^n on Sigma cap O and lambda := mu on O are finite Borel measures
lambda = nu.withDensity (1_M theta), using mu(O minus spt mu) = 0
Besicovitch: lambda(B_r(y))/nu(B_r(y)) -> 1_M theta (y) for nu-a.e. y (rnDeriv of a withDensity)
multiply by nu(B_r(y))/(omega_n r^n) -> 1 to get Theta(y) = 1_M theta (y) nu-a.e.
transfer to mu-a.e. on O via lambda << nu and mu(M^c) = 0

subproblems.title: mu_V-null subsets of the carrier are H^n-null
subproblems.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, U a subset of R^(n+l) and V = v(M, theta) a rectifiable n-varifold in U (M := V.carrier, theta := V.mult with theta > 0 on M and theta AEMeasurable for H^n restricted to M, mu := V.weight = (H^n restricted to M).withDensity (ofReal o theta), H^n := muHE[n]). If A is a subset of M with mu(A) = 0, then H^n(A) = 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ n ℓ : ℕ, ∀ (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (A : Set (Amb n ℓ)), A ⊆ V.carrier → V.weight A = 0 → (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) A = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: fact (F2) of the parent-supplied proof ('mu = theta H^n restricted to M with theta > 0 on M, so ... mu(S cap M) = 0 iff H^n(S cap M) = 0'), used in its steps 6(a) and 10.
1. Let A' := toMeasurable mu A. Then A' is measurable, A is contained in A', and mu(A') = mu(A) = 0 (measure_toMeasurable).
2. By definition of mu as a withDensity measure and measurability of A', 0 = mu(A') = lintegral over A' of ofReal(theta) d(H^n restricted to M) (withDensity_apply). The integrand ofReal o theta is AEMeasurable for H^n restricted to M (structure field aemeasurable_mult composed with ENNReal.ofReal), hence for its restriction to A'. A lower Lebesgue integral of an AEMeasurable function vanishes iff the function vanishes a.e. (lintegral_eq_zero_iff'), so ofReal(theta(x)) = 0 for a.e. x with respect to nu' := (H^n restricted to M) restricted to A'.
3. H^n restricted to M is concentrated on M because M is H^n-null-measurable (structure field nullMeasurableSet_carrier, ae_restrict_mem_0); so nu'-a.e. x lies in M (ae_restrict_of_ae). For x in M, theta(x) > 0 (structure field mult_pos), hence ofReal(theta(x)) > 0. Combining with step 2, nu'-a.e. x satisfies a contradiction, i.e. nu'(R^(n+l)) = 0.
4. nu'(R^(n+l)) = (H^n restricted to M)(A') = H^n(A' cap M) (Measure.restrict_apply with A' measurable). So H^n(A' cap M) = 0.
5. A is contained in A' (step 1) and in M (hypothesis), hence in A' cap M, and by monotonicity H^n(A) <= H^n(A' cap M) = 0.
proof_key_steps: take a measurable mu-null hull A' of A
mu(A') = integral over A' of ofReal theta d(H^n restricted to M) = 0 forces theta <= 0 a.e. there
theta > 0 on M and H^n restricted to M is concentrated on M give H^n(A' cap M) = 0
A is contained in A' cap M

subproblems.title: Carrier and support agree up to H^n-null sets on a measurable set inside U where the density is at least one
subproblems.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, U a subset of R^(n+l), V = v(M, theta) a rectifiable n-varifold in U with weight mu and support Sigma := V.support = U cap spt mu (H^n := muHE[n]), and O a measurable subset of R^(n+l) with O contained in U. Assume (b) for almost every y with respect to H^n restricted to Sigma cap O, y not in M implies V.HasDensity y 0; and (c) every y in Sigma cap O has some real Theta >= 1 with V.HasDensity y Theta. Then H^n((M cap O) symmetric-difference (Sigma cap O)) = 0.

Source: step 10 of the parent-supplied proof (theta = 1 H^n-a.e. on M cap O by (F2); mu(S cap O) = H^n(S cap O cap M) = H^n(S cap O cap Sigma)).
1. Let N := {x in M cap O : theta(x) != 1}. The hypothesis says mu({x : x in O and theta(x) != 1}) = 0, and N is contained in this set, so mu(N) = 0. As N is contained in M, the sibling lemma dohr_lmo_hausdorff_null_of_weight_null gives H^n(N) = 0.
2. Let S be a measurable set. Then (mu restricted to O)(S) = mu(S cap O) (Measure.restrict_apply) = lintegral over S cap O of ofReal(theta) d(H^n restricted to M) (withDensity_apply, S cap O measurable) = lintegral of ofReal(theta) with respect to H^n restricted to X, where X := (S cap O) cap M (Measure.restrict_restrict, S cap O measurable).
3. For a.e. x with respect to H^n restricted to X: x in X (X is H^n-null-measurable because S cap O is measurable and M is H^n-null-measurable; ae_restrict_mem_0), and x not in N (the restricted measure of N is at most H^n(N) = 0). For such x, x in M cap O and x not in N, so theta(x) = 1 and ofReal(theta(x)) = 1. Hence the integral in step 2 equals the integral of 1, i.e. H^n(X) = H^n(S cap O cap M).
4. Let Y := S cap O cap Sigma. X symmetric-difference Y = S cap ((M cap O) symmetric-difference (Sigma cap O)), which is contained in (M cap O) symmetric-difference (Sigma cap O), so H^n(X symmetric-difference Y) = 0. Then H^n(X) <= H^n(Y) + H^n(X minus Y) = H^n(Y) and H^n(Y) <= H^n(X) + H^n(Y minus X) = H^n(X), so H^n(X) = H^n(Y).
5. (H^n restricted to Sigma cap O)(S) = H^n(S cap (Sigma cap O)) = H^n(Y) (Measure.restrict_apply, S measurable).

subproblems.title: Transport of a null carrier-support symmetric difference into graph coordinates
subproblems.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, M and S subsets of R^(n+l), xi in R^(n+l), R and s reals with s <= R, Q a linear isometry equivalence of R^(n+l), u : R^n -> R^l any function, G(x) := graphPoint x (u x), Gamma := graphOver u (Bo^n_R(0)) (H^n := muHE[n]). Assume Q((S - xi)) cap Bo_R(0) = Gamma cap Bo_R(0) and H^n((M cap Bo_s(xi)) symmetric-difference (S cap Bo_s(xi))) = 0. Then for every rho with 0 < rho <= s, H^n((Q((M - xi)) cap Bo_rho(0)) symmetric-difference graphOver u W_rho) = 0, where W_rho := {x in Bo^n_rho(0) : ||graphPoint x (u x)|| < rho}.

Source: step 12 of the parent-supplied proof (carrier versus graph on Bo_rho(0)); the inclusion Bo^n_rho(0) in Bo^n_R(0) only needs rho <= R.
1. Let T(z) := Q(z - xi). T is an isometric bijection of R^(n+l) with ||T z|| = ||z - xi||, T(X) = Q '' ((fun x => x - xi) '' X) for every X, and T^{-1}(Bo_rho(0)) = Bo_rho(xi). As T is an isometry, H^n(T(X)) = H^n(X) for every X (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image), and as T is injective, T(X) symmetric-difference T(Y) = T(X symmetric-difference Y) (image of a difference under an injective map is the difference of images).
2. T(M) cap Bo_rho(0) = T(M cap Bo_rho(xi)): w lies in the left side iff w = T z with z in M and ||z - xi|| = ||T z|| < rho.
3. graphOver u W_rho = Gamma cap Bo_rho(0). Norm fact: ||graphPoint a b||^2 = ||a||^2 + ||b||^2 (split the coordinate sum over Fin (n+l) into the first n and last l indices), so ||a|| <= ||graphPoint a b||. (Inclusion one) If x in W_rho then ||x|| < rho <= s <= R, so x in Bo^n_R(0), G(x) in Gamma and ||G(x)|| < rho. (Inclusion two) If G(x) with x in Bo^n_R(0) satisfies ||G(x)|| < rho, then ||x|| <= ||G(x)|| < rho, so x in W_rho.
4. Gamma cap Bo_rho(0) = Gamma cap Bo_R(0) cap Bo_rho(0) (as rho <= R, Bo_rho(0) is contained in Bo_R(0)) = T(S) cap Bo_R(0) cap Bo_rho(0) (hypothesis) = T(S) cap Bo_rho(0) = T(S cap Bo_rho(xi)) (as in step 2).
5. By steps 2-4 and step 1, the set in the claim equals T(M cap Bo_rho(xi)) symmetric-difference T(S cap Bo_rho(xi)) = T((M cap Bo_rho(xi)) symmetric-difference (S cap Bo_rho(xi))), whose H^n-measure equals H^n((M cap Bo_rho(xi)) symmetric-difference (S cap Bo_rho(xi))). Since rho <= s, Bo_rho(xi) is contained in Bo_s(xi), and (M cap Bo_rho(xi)) symmetric-difference (S cap Bo_rho(xi)) = ((M cap Bo_s(xi)) symmetric-difference (S cap Bo_s(xi))) cap Bo_rho(xi), whose H^n-measure is 0 by hypothesis and monotonicity.
